item.title: China urges US, Israel to halt Middle East fighting, warns of 'vicious cycle'
item.description:
China on Monday urged all parties in the Middle East conflict, particularly the United States and Israel, to cease military operations, warning that continued fighting risks a "vicious cycle" that could plunge the region into chaos and drag down the global economy, according to Reuters.

The warning came as President Donald Trump extended a 48-hour deadline he had imposed on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, postponing threatened strikes on Iranian power plants for five days amid what he described as "very good and productive" conversations. Tehran denied any negotiations had taken place, with Iranian state media claiming Trump "withdrew his 48-hour ultimatum out of fear of Iran's response".

item.title: Antarctic microbes survive from -20°C to 75°C by feeding on air
item.description: Microorganisms buried in Antarctic soil can sustain themselves by feeding on trace gases in the atmosphere across a temperature range spanning 95 degrees Celsius, from minus 20°C to 75°C, according to new research from Australia's Monash University published in The ISME Journal.

item.title: Estee Lauder confirms merger talks with Spain's Puig
item.description:
Estée Lauder confirmed Monday that it is in discussions over a potential business combination with Puig, the Barcelona-based beauty group behind Charlotte Tilbury, Carolina Herrera, and Jean Paul Gaultier. The deal, first reported by the Financial Times, could be announced as soon as Monday and would create a combined entity valued at more than $40 billion, according to reports from Bloomberg and Investing.com.

In a statement, Estée Lauder said the two companies would "potentially merge their businesses," but cautioned that "no final decision has been made, and no agreement has been reached". Puig separately confirmed that negotiations are underway. Shares of Estée Lauder fell as much as 9.1% on the news, while Puig's stock rose roughly 3%.

item.title: Pakistan emerges as lead mediator between US and Iran
item.description:
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke by phone with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday, expressing solidarity with the Iranian people amid the ongoing war in the Gulf region and calling for urgent collective efforts to de-escalate tensions through dialogue and diplomacy.

The call came as Pakistan positioned itself as a lead mediator between the United States and Iran, with the Financial Times reporting that Pakistani army chief Asim Munir spoke directly with President Donald Trump on Sunday about the conflict. Senior Pakistani officials have been back-channeling communications between Tehran and Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to the Financial Times, with Pakistan pitching Islamabad as a possible venue for talks as early as this week.

item.title: Bahrain seeks UN approval of force to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
The UN Security Council on Monday began consultations on a draft resolution that would authorize the use of military force to secure the Strait of Hormuz, as a growing coalition of nations declared their willingness to help reopen the vital waterway that Iran has effectively shut down since late February.

The draft, circulated by Bahrain, invokes Chapter VII of the UN Charter — which grants the council authority to sanction actions ranging from targeted sanctions to the use of force — and would permit member states to employ "all necessary means" in and around the strait, according to a text seen by Reuters. The mandate would extend to the territorial waters of bordering states, with the aim of ensuring transit passage and deterring attempts to disrupt international navigation.

item.title: Chevron CEO says oil market underpricing Hormuz closure
item.description:
Chevron CEO Mike Wirth said Monday that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has inflicted greater damage on global oil and gas markets than the Russia-Ukraine war, warning that rebuilding supply chains and inventories will take considerable time even after the critical waterway reopens.

"We've got a lot of oil and gas now that is not flowing into the market," Wirth said at the CERAWeek by S&P Global conference in Houston. "Physical supply chains don't respond immediately, so even if the strait opens at some point, it will take time to rebuild inventories of the right grades of crude and the right types of fuel."

item.title: Israel used Iran's own street cameras to track and kill Khamenei
item.description:
Israel exploited Tehran's vast network of street cameras — hacked years earlier — to track Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and confirm his location before the February 28 airstrike that killed him, according to an Associated Press investigation published Monday based on interviews with intelligence officials familiar with the operation.

The revelation underscores how surveillance infrastructure built by authoritarian governments to monitor dissent can be turned into a weapon against them.

item.title: Claude can now point, click and navigate your Mac like a human user
item.description: Anthropic is rolling out new capabilities that allow its Claude AI to directly control Mac computers, pointing, clicking, and navigating applications the way a human user would. The update, arriving March 23 for Claude Pro and Max subscribers as a research preview, brings computer-use features to both Claude Cowork and Claude Code on macOS.

item.title: Colombian military plane crashes after takeoff, killing at least one
item.description:
A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane carrying 125 people crashed moments after takeoff Monday morning in the country's remote southern Amazon region, killing at least one person, injuring 77 others, and leaving more than 40 still unaccounted for as rescue operations continued into the evening.

The aircraft went down about two kilometers from the airport in Puerto Leguízamo, a municipality in the Amazonian province of Putumayo near the borders of Peru and Ecuador, according to Defense Minister Pedro Sánchez, who disclosed the crash on X and called it a "tragic accident." The Lockheed Martin-built plane was transporting 114 soldiers and 11 crew members to another city in Putumayo province when it encountered an unspecified problem and plunged to the ground.

item.title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf ID'd as Trump negotiation partner
item.description:
Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has been identified by U.S. and Israeli sources as the Iranian official at the center of talks with American envoys, even as Tehran flatly denies any negotiations are taking place and Ghalibaf himself dismissed the reports as "fake news."

President Donald Trump announced Monday that he was ordering a five-day pause on planned strikes against Iran's power plants and energy infrastructure, saying the U.S. had held "very good and productive conversations" with Iranian counterparts over the preceding two days. Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner had been in discussions with "a top person" in Iran but refused to identify the individual, saying he did not want that person to be killed.

item.title: Australia, EU poised to finalize free trade deal after nearly a decade of talks
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Australia on Monday for a three-day visit aimed at concluding a free trade agreement that has been under negotiation since 2018. Von der Leyen is set to meet Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Tuesday, with both sides signaling they are close to finalizing a deal that would also include a new security and defense partnership.

item.title: Oil prices swing as Iran denies Trump's claim of war talks
item.description: Oil prices swung wildly on Monday as President Donald Trump claimed the United States held "productive conversations" with Iran aimed at ending the four-week-old war, only for Tehran to flatly deny any negotiations took place. The conflicting signals sent crude benchmarks tumbling from recent highs before partially recovering, while Wall Street rallied on hopes for a diplomatic resolution.

item.title: ISS images of Russian missile strike on Kyiv verified by analysts
item.description:
Images taken from the International Space Station appear to show Russian ballistic missiles streaking toward Kyiv and being intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses, offering a rare space-based view of the war that has gripped analysts and the public alike.

The photographs, captured by an ISS-mounted camera on December 27, 2025, show two luminous trails moving from the northeast toward the Ukrainian capital before vanishing amid bursts of explosions in and around the city. The footage was compiled into a timelapse by Italian space enthusiast Riccardo Rossi of the AstronautiCAST YouTube channel and first published on February 23, 2026, quickly spreading through Ukrainian open-source intelligence channels on the eve of the war's fourth anniversary.

item.title: AWS Bahrain region disrupted by drones for second time this month
item.description:
Amazon said on Monday that its Amazon Web Services cloud computing region in Bahrain has "been disrupted" due to drone activity, marking the second time the facility has been hit since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran earlier this month.

The disruption was first reported by Reuters, with an Amazon spokesperson confirming that the outage stemmed from drone activity in the area. Amazon said it is helping to migrate customers to alternate AWS regions while it works to recover, though the company did not disclose the extent of the damage or provide a timeline for restoration.

"As this situation evolves and, as we have advised before, we request those with workloads in the affected regions continue to migrate to other locations," Amazon said in a statement Monday night.

item.title: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes near Tonga; no tsunami threat
item.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Tonga in the South Pacific on Tuesday, according to the United States Geological Survey, but the deep tremor prompted no tsunami warning and there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.

item.title: Sunken Soviet sub is leaking radioactive material, study finds
item.description: Two Cold War-era nuclear hazards — a cracking concrete dome in the Marshall Islands and a corroding Soviet submarine on the floor of the Norwegian Sea — are drawing renewed scientific attention as researchers document ongoing radioactive releases into the world's oceans.

item.title: China mapping ocean floor for submarine warfare, Reuters finds
item.description: China is conducting a vast undersea mapping and monitoring operation across the Pacific, Indian, and Arctic oceans, building detailed knowledge of marine conditions that naval experts say would be crucial for waging submarine warfare against the United States and its allies, according to a Reuters investigation published Monday.

item.title: Iran hits Tel Aviv with cluster missiles as war enters fourth week
item.description: Iran fired fresh waves of missiles into central Israel on Tuesday, striking areas near Tel Aviv and Haifa with cluster munitions, as Tehran dismissed President Donald Trump's claims of ongoing peace negotiations as "fake news" — a contradiction that sent oil prices surging after a brief reprieve.

item.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel as IRGC rejects Trump's peace talk claims
item.description: Iran fired several missile salvos at Israel overnight Monday into Tuesday, striking areas in Tel Aviv, Haifa, and northern Israel, even as President Donald Trump insisted that "very strong" peace talks with Tehran were underway — claims Iranian officials flatly denied.

item.title: SMFG preparing possible takeover of Jefferies, FT reports
item.description:
Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group is working on plans for a potential takeover of Jefferies Financial Group, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday that sent Jefferies shares sharply higher in premarket trading.

SMFG, Japan's second-largest lender, has assembled a small internal team tasked with monitoring conditions and positioning the bank to act should Jefferies' depressed share price present a compelling opportunity, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Jefferies shares climbed roughly 9.5% in U.S. premarket trading on Tuesday, while Frankfurt-listed shares had already jumped 6% following the report. SMFG shares closed up 2.78% in Tokyo.
